title: Introduce signal-weighted profile rollups and compact release summaries
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a signal-weighted rollup pipeline that consolidates per-snapshot performance profiles into compact, deterministic rollups and auto-generates short release summaries (1-3 lines) highlighting top regressions and recommended mitigations. Backwards compatible; enables smaller changelog bundles and faster on-call triage.
description:
Context and motivation: model onboarding currently produces verbose per-snapshot performance profiles which are expensive to store and noisy for release notes. ENG-904 requested a way to surface the most actionable changes in a deterministic, compact form that preserves provenance. This PR implements a signal-weighted rollup and a compact release-summarizer that converts rollups into short human-readable briefs.

Design summary: the rollup pipeline aggregates recent profile snapshots for a model variant using configurable signal weights (traffic volume, recency decay, tail-latency contribution, error-rate multiplier). Each metric is merged using occupancy-scaled percentiles and a deterministic downsampling seed so rollups are stable across replays. Rollup metadata includes provenance hashes and the list of contributing snapshots. The release summarizer uses delta heuristics with a severity scoring function to emit up to three sentences: overall trend, top regression (metric + shard/route), and recommended mitigation (quantize/rollforward/rollback). Summaries include links to the full rollup blob and an opt-in compact diff for triage.

What changed (high level): added registry/core/rollup.py implementing weighted aggregation and provenance tagging; added registry/cli/onboard_rollup.py to emit rollups during onboarding; added tools/changelog/summarizer.py to synthesize compact release briefs; added integration tests under tests/rollup_integration_test.py; added unit tests for weighting heuristics and deterministic sampling; updated docs/content/onboarding-rollups.md with configuration examples and recommended defaults; added CI job step to validate rollup determinism under seed permutations.

Checklist: - [x] Implement signal-weighted aggregation algorithm and provenance tags - [x] Deterministic downsampling seed and replay tests - [x] Compact summarizer with 1-3 sentence output and links - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and CLI flags for weight tuning and retention - [x] Add migration to backfill recent snapshots as optional job

Testing notes: local unit tests cover percentile merge math and seed determinism; integration test creates synthetic snapshots with staged traffic profiles and validates summary severity ranking matches expected order for known regressions. CI initially failed on an edge-case percentile interpolation (flake) which I fixed by switching to occupancy-weighted interpolation and re-ran the pipeline. All checks passed on the final run.

Backward compatibility and migration: rollups are opt-in until the onboard flag is flipped; the rollup blobs are stored alongside existing raw snapshots and referenced by new compact-changelog records. A backfill job (scripts/migration/backfill_rollups.py) is included but gated and documented. There are no breaking changes to existing consumer APIs.

Operational notes: default weights are conservative (traffic:0.6, recency_decay:0.25, error_multiplier:0.15). We recommend enabling rollups for high-traffic variants first. Rollup generation is CPU-bound but runs incrementally; added autoscale hint to the Dedicated runtime docs for short jobs.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2024-11-12 after approvals from Priya and Jared. Follow-ups planned: ENG-921 (UX templates for release briefs) and a follow-up to expose per-route summaries in the Console (tracked as ENG-950).

review_comments: Jared Smith: Why use a fixed seed instead of per-model entropy? Response: fixed seed with model+variant salt yields deterministic but stable sampling; added unit tests to prove bit-for-bit equality across replays.

Priya Nambiar: Can we avoid storing full snapshots twice? Response: rollup blobs are stored as deduplicated pointers; backfill is optional. Updated migration docs to clarify storage impact (~5-8% additional storage for first week).
Omar Reyes: CI found flaky percentile edge-case — suggested occupancy interpolation. Response: switched interpolation algo and added deterministic sample harness; CI green on re-run.
